note: Launch snapshot. Entries whose source is null are declared but not yet published; fetching them fails with a clear error.

components.name: interpreter
components.description: The default local interpreter model: Gemma 4 E4B instruction-tuned (Google, Gemma Terms of Use), fetched from its upstream repository pinned to an exact revision and run in-process in bfloat16 (about 15 GB of weights, about 16 GB of peak VRAM). Asked one narrow question per component (multi-call mode); one to one and a half minutes per description on a 24 GB-class card. The upstream repository is gated: accept its terms and set CHARACTER_FACTORY_AUTH_TOKEN to an access token for that account, or configure another local model or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint instead.

components.name: make-figure
components.description: Text-to-identity, generative: samples 45 identity coefficients plus six skeletal-proportion controls from the prompt's distribution (joint rectified flow around a semantic center; seeded, CPU-noise reproducible); resting expression is authored as exact zeros.

interpretation.fields: one dense physique-first sentence in plain modern English: sex/age words first, then height, overall build and body fat, musculature, and face/head structure (jaw, cheeks, brow). Physique vocabulary only — no name, occupation, clothing, era, scene, or style words.

components.name: make-skin

inference.prompt_template: MHR face albedo texture map, neutral delit lighting, {prompt}

interpretation.fields: comma-separated fields: ALWAYS state a natural-language skin tone first (like 'light-medium neutral-toned skin' or 'deep warm-toned skin'; an optional 'MST <1-10>' code may FOLLOW it) — use the description's own complexion when it gives one; otherwise CHOOSE a demographically plausible tone for the stated nationality, ancestry, or ethnicity, with natural person-to-person variation; a tone may be left unstated only when the description explicitly asks for that. Then: age, gender presentation, ancestry, brow character, facial structure, lips, pores/wrinkles, optional skin conditions — and when the description gives no facial features, invent SPECIFIC plausible ones fitting the character's demographics, age, and life, never generic placeholders; never clothing, hair, or body-shape/silhouette words

components.description: Full-body skin albedo on the body's canonical UV atlas.

components.name: make-eye

inference.prompt_template: Full UV eye albedo texture map, {prompt}

interpretation.fields: comma-separated fields: iris color, radial fiber character, limbal ring, pupil, sclera tone, sclera veins; conservative natural defaults for anything unstated

components.description: Eye albedo (iris/sclera) applied to both placed eyeballs.

components.name: make-garment

inference.prompt_template: mhrgarment, form-fitting garment uv texture map. Clothing requested: {prompt}.

interpretation.fields: the outfit worn on the body (garments only — footwear belongs to the shoe slot): a complete outfit — top and bottom, or one full-body garment — inventing pieces appropriate to the character when the description does not specify clothing; when it does, follow it exactly and add nothing beyond it; each item with its textile/material character, comma-separated

components.description: Garment albedo painted over an unoccupied background; its keyed coverage becomes the character's garment shell mesh.

components.name: make-shoe

inference.prompt_template: mhrshoe, canonical one-foot shoe UV albedo texture, {prompt}, fixed layout with {shaft_clause}, upper-foot island at upper right, sole island at lower right, dark charcoal outside
inference.shaft_clause_empty: empty leg or shaft island on the left
inference.shaft_clause_shafted: {percent}% shaft height, leg or shaft island on the left

interpretation.fields: the footwear's design/construction, material, color palette, and finish or pattern, comma-separated — chosen to suit the character when the description names none; boots and shafted styles are supported — name the style plainly (flip flops, sandals, loafers, sneakers, high tops, ankle boots, mid boots, tall boots)

components.description: Footwear painted on the component's one-foot canvas; its foot chart maps the canvas onto both feet, and the mapped coverage becomes the character's shoe shell mesh. Supported styles range from below-ankle shoes to tall boots (the shaft is cut to each style's declared height), declared here so the interpreter clamps footwear prompts accordingly.

components.name: body-rig
components.description: The rig of 1.1.0 (same pinned MHR release) plus the LOD3 render topology: MHR's own LOD3 with its supplied barycentric map, transferred skin weights and expression morphs, the authored eye and mouth apertures, and the LOD3 mouth block with its own measured animation-limitation table. Patch: expression semantics re-derived on the render topology, each numeric claim naming its metric.

components.name: assembly-assets
components.description: 0.2.0's files with the launch-tier interior meshes: 300-triangle eyeballs, 700-triangle dental arches, a 400-triangle tongue (never omitted). Lashes and caruncles are omitted at this tier.

components.name: make-wig
components.description: The default hair provider: a procedural wig synthesizer consuming the character's semantic hair block and the assembled head/body geometry. Vendored in the package; this entry records versions for provenance and future model-driven variants.

components.name: flux2-klein-base-4b
components.description: FLUX.2 Klein 4B, undistilled base (Black Forest Labs, Apache-2.0): transformer + text encoder + VAE. The texture adapters were trained against this base; the identity component shares its text encoder.

components.name: flux2-klein-4b
components.description: FLUX.2 Klein 4B, distilled (Black Forest Labs, Apache-2.0): the fast turbo variant adopted by bake-time turbo mode.
